title: Sebastian and the Hollow Anew
premise: In the city of Vellamere, where magic was outlawed after the Hollowing, bone-carver Rosalind Marchetti survives by selling charms that carry only whispers of her gift. When a mute boy named Sebastian appears at her door speaking a language older than any kingdom, she discovers he carries the memory of King Aldous — whose crown has been worn for five years by the Hollow, an entity that devours inheritance itself. To free the king and stop the Hollow from consuming every bloodline's past, Rosalind must teach Sebastian to wield his inherited tongue before the boy's own memories are eaten. In the end, Rosalind binds the Hollow into her own carved bones at the cost of hearing the dead forever, while Sebastian, carrying the restored king's memories, becomes the living archive of everything the city tried to forget.
about_author: Coral Thornbury is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent a decade restoring medieval reliquaries before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about objects that remember and people who wish they could forget.

chapters.title: The Quiet Trade
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. We meet her carving a mourning charm for a grieving widow, hiding the fact that she truly hears the dead. The emotional beat is weary self-erasure: survival means shrinking her gift to nothing.

chapters.title: A Knock Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A barefoot boy, Sebastian, appears at her door during a curfew raid, speaking a language no one alive should know. When he touches her carvings, the dead go silent — then speak through him. Beat: fear sharpening into recognition.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She tests Sebastian with a relic femur; it recites the coronation of King Aldous — including the moment something entered the crown. Beat: dawning horror as she realizes the 'madness' that ended magic began in the palace.

chapters.title: The Law of Ash
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, first time. Through his eyes we see how memories arrive unbidden, and how the Wardens of Ash hunt anyone who carries old words. He trusts Rosalind because she doesn't flinch from him. Beat: fragile belonging.

chapters.title: The Warden's Ledger
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Warden Ilsa Corvane raids the market district with a ledger of names of the magically marked. Rosalind buys safety with a false charm and learns Sebastian's description is already circulating. Beat: the price of shelter rising.

chapters.title: Five Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Flashback chapters surface: he fled the palace the night of the Hollowing, the king's memories sealed inside him by a dying court sorceress. Beat: grief for a childhood spent running from his own head.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Debt
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She seeks out Odric, an exiled scholar who maps magical debts, who confirms the Hollow feeds on inheritance — bloodlines are forgetting their dead across the city. Beat: stakes widen from one boy to everyone.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Rosalind teaches Sebastian to control the language instead of being ridden by it; the dead begin coaching him too. A tender chapter of found family. Beat: hope, deliberately placed before the fall.

chapters.title: Ilsa at the Door
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Warden Corvane arrives not to arrest but to bargain: her own daughter's memories are fading, eaten by the Hollow. She offers a blind eye if Rosalind can save the girl. Beat: enemy revealed as fellow sufferer.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Forgot Her Mother
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He draws out what remains of Corvane's daughter's memories and fails — the Hollow has already digested them. His first true defeat. Beat: guilt, and the realization that time is shorter than anyone thought.

chapters.title: Beneath the Palace of Salt
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Guided by the dead, they enter the flooded undercrofts beneath the palace where the Hollow nests inside the crowned, hollow-eyed king Aldous. First sight of the antagonist. Beat: dread made flesh.

chapters.title: The Crown Speaks
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The Hollow addresses Sebastian directly, offering to return his stolen childhood if he surrenders the king's memories. It shows him his mother's face. Beat: temptation rendered almost irresistible.

chapters.title: Odric's Betrayal
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Odric sells their location to the Wardens to buy back his own erased family name — proving the Hollow's reach extends through human greed. Capture, escape through the salt tunnels. Beat: trust shattered.

chapters.title: Ashfall
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The city-wide purge begins; charms burn in the square, and the dead grow quieter as more bloodlines are severed. Rosalind chooses open rebellion, carving weapons instead of trinkets. Beat: resolve hardened by loss.

chapters.title: The Sorceress's Last Word
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Among the dead he finally finds the court sorceress who sealed him, who reveals the binding's flaw: the Hollow can be imprisoned in bone willingly given, but the giver loses what the bone holds. Beat: understanding the true cost.

chapters.title: Corvane's Choice
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Ilsa must decide between her oath and her daughter's remaining memories; she burns her ledger and joins them, giving Rosalind access to the palace above. Beat: alliance forged from shared ruin.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the throne room, Sebastian speaks the unbinding while Rosalind carves a prison-bone in real time. King Aldous surfaces briefly, lucid, begging them not to save him at the boy's expense. Beat: climax begins, love against necessity.

chapters.title: What the Hollow Offers
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The Hollow floods him with every memory it has ever eaten — whole generations — offering godhood through inheritance. He nearly drowns in other people's lives. Beat: the darkest hour, identity dissolving.

chapters.title: Bone of My Bone
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind completes the carving using her own wrist-bone, willingly given, and speaks the binding in Sebastian's ancient tongue. The Hollow pours into the bone; her connection to the dead dies with the sealing. Beat: sacrifice fulfilled.

chapters.title: The King Who Remained
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Freed, Aldous abdicates rather than rule a city that outlawed magic to survive him, entrusting his memories to Sebastian formally. The purge ends; the Wardens stand down. Beat: bittersweet restoration.

chapters.title: Silence, and What Grows There
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Months later, Rosalind cannot hear the dead anymore — the silence is enormous. But Sebastian remembers everything now, and when she needs her mother's voice, he gives it back to her word for word. Beat: grief transmuted into inheritance.

chapters.title: Sebastian and the Hollow Anew
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, closing frame. He opens a small school where children learn the old language safely, the bound Hollow-bone kept as a warning on the mantel. Rosalind carves again, ordinary things, for living hands. Final beat: memory survives not in bones or crowns, but in who we choose to tell.
